correctness.rationale: PASS: The final statement is for synchronous Rule 54 on indexed cyclic rings n>=3, not quotient rings. Temporal columns a,b,c satisfy b_(j+1)=b_j XOR(a_j OR c_j). The exact (a,b)->(b,c) transition constructs a finite graph of 2^(2t) vertices, and rooted spatial closed walks of length n correspond bijectively to Fix(F_n^t). Independently compiled and executed a fresh table-driven C++ graph generator and zero-in/out peeling for t=1,3,5,7,9,11, enumerating all 4,194,304 vertices at t=11 and all 4,192,256 edges. Reproduced edge totals 2,56,992,16256,261632,4192256 and residual permutation-core cycle lengths (1),(1),(1),(1),(1),(1,11,11). No directed closed walk can lie outside the peeled core, and surviving in/out degree exactly one means the core is a disjoint cycle union. Thus counts 1 for the five lower odd iterates, and 1+22*1_(11|n) for iterate eleven. Since 11 is prime, the 22 nonzero eleven-site states give two primitive temporal orbits of length 11; the two given binary words translate by shifts +4 and -4, related by reflection. All-n theorem follows from complete finite temporal-column graph exhaustion, NOT from checking only rings through n=11. The theorem makes no statement about odd t>=13.
